tagline: Building great companies for the long term
hero_kpi_rationale: NAV per share is the master KPI for Exor because it is a holding whose value is determined by the performance of its strategic investments, notably Ferrari. This KPI directly captures shareholder value creation.

kpis.name: Net asset value per share
kpis.explanation: Total asset value minus liabilities, divided by number of shares outstanding.
kpis.description: NAV per share increased 9.0% in 2024, driven by Ferrari performance, despite underperformance versus MSCI World.

kpis.name: EBITDA margin
kpis.explanation: Consolidated EBITDA margin of portfolio companies, calculated as EBITDA divided by revenues.
kpis.description: Ferrari's EBITDA margin reached 38% in 2024, reflecting its industrial strength and premium positioning.

kpis.name: Consolidated net revenues
kpis.explanation: Total revenues generated by key portfolio companies, primarily Ferrari.
kpis.description: Ferrari generated 6.7 billion euros in revenues in 2024, up 12%, driven by new launches and sustained demand.

kpis.name: EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, primarily from Ferrari.
kpis.description: Ferrari generated 2.6 billion euros in EBITDA in 2024, confirming its operational strength.

kpis.name: Capital expenditures
kpis.explanation: Fixed asset spending to modernize or expand operational capacity.
kpis.description: No detailed CAPEX investment data provided in the consolidated report.

kpis.name: Total headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees across portfolio companies.
kpis.description: Consolidated employee count not disclosed in annual report.

kpis.name: Total assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of 37.13 billion euros in latest year

kpis.name: Total debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of 3.67 billion euros in latest year

kpis.name: Leapmotor revenues
kpis.explanation: Revenues generated by Leapmotor, a joint venture with Stellantis, specialist in electric vehicles in China.
kpis.description: Leapmotor exceeded 4 billion euros in revenues in 2024, with growth over 90% and gross margin of 8.4%, reaching profitability in Q4.
kpis.signal: Explosive growth for Leapmotor in Chinese EV market.

kpis.name: Stellantis revenues
kpis.explanation: Total revenues of Stellantis, one of Exor's primary assets and global automotive leader.
kpis.description: Stellantis revenues declined to 156.9 billion euros in 2024 (-17% vs 2023), impacted by weak industry volumes, Chinese competition and internal operational challenges.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in 2024 due to external and internal headwinds.

risks.title: Electric vehicle transition and uncertain EV demand
risks.score_rationale: Major risk for Stellantis (40% of portfolio). Explicitly mentioned as key factor in 2024 decline: regulatory uncertainty, increased customer price sensitivity and reduced government incentives for EVs. Intensive language (challenging, struggling). Upward trend with Ram electric pause. Critical weight in transition strategy.

risks.title: Intensified competition from Chinese automakers
risks.score_rationale: Existential risk for Stellantis and CNH. Precise data: Chinese exports of electric passenger vehicles in 2024 totalled 1.3 million units, a year-on-year increase of 24%. Alarmist language (intensified competition, exerted downward pressure). Upward trend with penetration in Brazil, EU, Mexico. Direct impact on pricing and volumes.

risks.title: Product litigation risks and major recalls
risks.score_rationale: Philips paid $1.1 billion plus 540 million euros for Respironics recall. Mentioned as significant milestones but remains residual risk. Moderate language (resolved, clarity) but substantial amounts. Stable trend with resolution underway. Significant weight for Philips (10% of GAV).

risks.title: Agricultural cyclicality and commodity price decline
risks.score_rationale: CNH suffered 23% sales decline in 2024. Explicit language: cyclical downturn, reduced incomes driven by lower commodity prices. Regional data: Brazil and Europe weak, combines down 43% in EMEA. Upward risk trend. Significant weight (CNH in portfolio).

risks.title: Post-acquisition integration and operational challenges
risks.score_rationale: Clarivate suffering from integration issues from its previous strategy and Stellantis from large-scale retooling of factories. Moderate but repeated language (struggling, gaps in product lineup). Upward trend with CEO change at Clarivate. Moderate but rising weight.

risks.title: Leadership dependency and succession risks
risks.score_rationale: Carlos Tavares resigned in December 2024 at Stellantis; Gerrit Marx appointed CNH CEO in July 2024; Matti Shem Tov appointed Clarivate CEO in August 2024. Neutral language but frequent changes. Upward trend with three CEO changes in six months. Moderate but strategic weight.

risks.title: Chinese market slowdown and post-COVID normalization
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned for bioMérieux and Philips: softness in the Chinese market and further post-COVID normalisation led to weaker results. Moderate language (difficult year). Stable but persistent trend. Moderate weight for portfolio healthcare.

risks.title: Saturation and competition in data and software
risks.score_rationale: Clarivate facing ever-growing competition in all its markets and slowdown in end markets (IP filings, biotech funding). Moderate language (facing challenges). Upward trend with 40% stock price decline in 2024. Moderate weight (growth investment).

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence in the 2024 annual report. Exor does not position AI as a strategic lever for its portfolio companies.
evidence: No reference to AI or related technologies in strategy or innovation sections.
No AI-related KPIs or initiatives mentioned.
Technology discussions focus on electrification, vehicle platforms and product innovation (F80, Ferrari 12Cilindri, e-building).
